in.other_title: Bowman et al. reuse Parrish et al.'s time-limited QuALITY judging, swapping debate for model chat
in.rationale: The authors adopt the time-limited QuALITY setup from Parrish et al.'s debate studies and say what they change (model chat assistance instead of debate arguments), which fits EXTENDS. The link is to the two-turn paper because its judges also had a 5-minute limit; the single-turn study used a shorter limit.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Time-limited reading of QuALITY passages as a way to create an expertise gap for human judges; holds for the timed QuALITY condition only

open_obligations: Note that time limit, judge pool and number of turns changed together.
Check whether 5 minutes still leaves the passage largely unread.
Compare with pilot timing data used to set the 5-minute limit.
out.other_title: Artificial time limit for judges; 60-120 s pilot variations made virtually no difference
out.rationale: Parrish et al. note the 90-second limit is artificial and that 120 seconds might still be too short. The two-turn follow-up keeps the top 16 of 32 pilot judges and sets 5 minutes per judgment, and still reports no significant effect of arguments (2x2x2 ANOVA, no main effects); judge selection and counter-arguments also changed, so time is not isolated.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether a longer judging time changes the debate-argument null result, for human judges on 2-option QuALITY

text: Judges make a first judgment based only on the initial arguments and a second judgment additionally based on the counter-arguments. The paper keeps the top half (16 of 32) of pilot judges by post-passage performance and, from their pilot response times, sets a limit of 5 minutes per judgment in the main task.
title: Two-judgment protocol with selected Upwork judges and a 5-minute limit per judgment
